beats.narration_text: Ask Medhavy's tutor about equation one point one three, and it answers. It quotes your textbook. It points at the page the answer came from. But nobody ever trained it on your book. No one fed those chapters into an AI model. So how does it know?

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea, in one breath. The tutor never memorizes your textbook. Every time a student asks a question, it searches your book, finds the passages that match, and reads them right there in the moment. Then it lets them go. That search is what keeps every answer tied to your material.

lines: The tutor never memorizes your book.
It searches it, every single time.
That search is what keeps it grounded.
props.caption: The model is rented and unchanged. The book is yours, and it stays yours.

beats.narration_text: There are two ways a tutor could know your book, and the difference matters to you. It could be trained in, baked into the model, where a single typo means a retraining run and you can never see what it drew on. Or your book can stay yours, sitting in an index the tutor searches. Medhavy works the second way.

props.title: Two ways a tutor could know your book.
props.leftHeader: if the book were trained in
leftItems: A typo needs a retraining run
You cannot see what it used
rightItems: Your book stays in a searchable index
A typo is fixed in about a minute
You can see the passages it used
props.visualBrief: Both columns fill the safe area and build in PAIRS so each line reads as a direct comparison. The divider draws down between them. The right column takes teal only in the last quarter; the left stays full-strength ink, never faded.

beats.narration_text: So what actually happens the moment a student presses enter? First a quick check: does this even need the book? Then the system decides how to teach the answer. Then it searches your textbook and pulls out the closest passages. Only after all of that does anything reach an AI, with those passages sitting above the question.

props.title: Four steps, and only the last one is AI.

steps.label: Check
steps.sub: does this even need the book?

props.footnote: The first three steps run on our own machine. No AI is involved until the fourth.
props.visualBrief: Four boxes spanning the full safe width, connectors drawing between them in narration order. A visible gap opens after step three so three-of-ours-then-the-AI reads as a gap rather than a list. Footnote at 32px, readable on a phone.

beats.narration_text: In one file. Every time your site is built, your chapters are cut into small pieces and written into a single index. Here is one of those pieces. Ordinary text, the section it came from, and a line of labels. That line is there because students type equation one point one three, and a search engine does not read that as a word.

props.filename: the index - one piece of your book
props.visualBrief: The record reveals line by line. The keywords line takes the accent and holds - that is the beat's one idea. Keep the code large enough to read on a phone.

show.event: the record reveals line by line on the eggshell ground

the accent holds through the explanation of why 1.13 is not a word

beats.narration_text: You can test all of this yourself. Fix a typo in a chapter, rebuild the site, and ask the tutor again. It is corrected in about a minute. A trained model would need a whole retraining run. And that same speed is the thing to watch: if the rebuild is ever skipped, the tutor keeps answering from the older book, quietly.

beats.narration_text: So grounded is not a slogan. It is a search that runs every single time a student asks. That is why a wrong answer is almost never the AI's fault, and why the first thing to check is simply whether the right page was found, and whether your index is current.

props.title: Grounded is not a slogan. It is a search.
leftItems: Answers tied to your own book
props.rightHeader: what to keep an eye on
rightItems: A stale index gives no warning
Check the sources when an answer looks wrong
props.visualBrief: The honest recap. Benefit and cost weighted equally - the caution column takes crimson, but the benefit column is never dimmed to make it stand out.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this to any course tool you already use, and ask it three things: when you answer from my material, where is that material actually stored, when was it last updated, and can you show me the exact passages you used? That last one is the question that bites. If a tool cannot show you its passages, you have no way to tell a grounded answer from a confident guess.
